sections.html:
Lake Champlain's eastern shore is where Burlington stands, roughly 45 miles below the Canadian line, and it serves as the Chittenden County seat. The 2020 census counted 44,743 residents, making it Vermont's most populous municipality. The land rises steeply from the lakeshore, and roughly a third of the city's 15.5 square miles is water.

Around 60 percent of residents rent, so rentals are a large share of the housing. The University of Vermont Medical Center and the University of Vermont employ the most people, and that brings steady demand from students and staff.

Neighborhoods shape what a house is like to sell:

  • Downtown, the commercial center around the Church Street Marketplace.
  • The Hill Section, described as the wealthiest neighborhood.
  • The Old North End, the oldest and most densely populated area.
  • The South End, a former industrial district now known for its arts scene.
  • The New North End, the most populous neighborhood.
  • The University District, near the University of Vermont and student housing.

A triple-decker in the Old North End and a single-family house in the New North End attract different buyers and carry different rules. Start any sale by naming the type of property you own.

sections.h2: Winter wear on an older house
sections.html:
Cold winters bring about 86 inches of snow and about 43 inches of precipitation a year. Inspectors and buyers start with the roof and any ice damming at the eaves, then check attic and basement insulation and air sealing, then look at how old the heating system is and what fuel it burns.

Many rental buildings here went up decades ago with little thought to weatherization. Owners of older houses who would rather not handle repairs before listing can sell as is for cash and skip fixing whatever an inspection turns up.

Four quarterly payments cover the year, each due on the 12th of August, November, March and June; a weekend 12th moves the due date to the next business day. The Clerk/Treasurer's Office takes payments and handles interest and penalties for a fiscal year that runs July 1 to June 30.

Your bill blends municipal tax with education tax. On the education side, a filed Homestead Declaration (Form HS-122) with no business or rental use earns the homestead education rate. A property that is not a primary residence pays the nonhomestead rate.

Every property is supposed to be valued at 100 percent of fair market value. If you think yours is too high, you can grieve it:

StepTiming
Appraisals take effectApril 1
Change of Assessment Notices mailedFirst week of May
Grievance deadline14 calendar days from the notice
Board of Assessors hearingsTypically third week of May
Appeal to Board of Tax Appeals14 days from the decision letter

Bring credible evidence that the value is too high, because a general belief will not persuade the Board of Assessors. You will find the Assessor's Office on the ground floor of City Hall, 149 Church Street.

A transfer of title triggers a Vermont property transfer tax. 32 V.S.A. chapter 231 puts the liability on the transferee, the buyer, unless the parties agree differently, and the purchase contract is where that is decided.

The state's rates include a 0.22 percent clean water surcharge:

  • A general rate of 1.25 percent, or 1.47 percent with the surcharge.
  • For a buyer's principal residence, 0.5 percent on the first $200,000, then 1.47 percent above that.
  • For year-round habitable property that is not the buyer's principal residence and is not a long-term rental, 3.40 percent, or 3.62 percent with the surcharge.
  • For principal residences financed in part through certain housing programs, the first $250,000 is exempt.

The return goes to the town clerk along with the deed, and the tax falls due within 30 days of closing. Since the rate follows the buyer's intended use, an investor purchasing a duplex has a different calculation from a family planning to live there.

sections.h2: Rental registration, vacant buildings and weatherization
sections.html:
The Permitting and Inspections Department enforces Burlington's Minimum Housing Ordinance, which requires rentals to be registered under Sec. 18-15 of the city code. Short-term and long-term rentals register through the city's online portal. The department also enforces a Vacant Building Ordinance (Chapter 8, Article 3) and issues building and zoning permits. Its office is at 645 Pine Street, phone 802-863-0442.

The Weatherization Ordinance adds a rule for high energy use rental buildings, those with total space heating use above 50,000 BTU per square foot per year. Owners must hire a BPI-certified contractor for an audit and then for the work. Re-inspection fees and fines follow if work is not completed on time, unless the department grants an extension or waiver.

You can check a building's status in the city's property database. A green bar means compliant and a yellow bar means not yet compliant.

If you own a rental that has not met these requirements, a cash buyer purchasing as is may take on the compliance work, which can be easier than finishing it yourself before a sale.

sections.h2: Can a Burlington homeowner add an accessory dwelling unit before selling?
sections.html:
An accessory dwelling unit is a permitted use where there is an owner-occupied single-family home. Section 5.4.5 of the city's zoning ordinance limits the unit to 900 square feet or 30 percent of the principal home's gross floor area, whichever is greater, and requires wastewater certification by the Department of Public Works.

Approval depends on owner occupancy. If neither unit is owner-occupied, the approval is void and the kitchen in the accessory unit must be removed within 90 days. A deed reference to the ADU permit must be recorded before the certificate of occupancy is issued.

That owner-occupancy rule matters before you sell. A buyer who plans to rent both units may not be able to keep an ADU approved on owner occupancy, so ask Planning and Zoning how the rule applies before you advertise the unit as income.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale fit a Burlington property?
sections.html:
A cash buyer skips the lender, so nothing waits on a mortgage approval. That is useful for a building with open rental registration questions, an energy compliance problem or an unfinished ADU, because the buyer prices the work into the offer instead of asking you to finish it.

Gather the property tax bill, any rental registration paperwork, permits and ADU records. Decide who will cover the transfer tax, since state law puts it on the buyer unless the contract says otherwise. Then compare the written offer with a regular listing.

faqs.q: How often is property tax due in Burlington, VT?
faqs.a: Four times a year. Installments are due on the 12th of August, November, March and June, or the next business day if the 12th falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: Who pays the Vermont property transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer, unless the parties agree otherwise. State law makes the tax the liability of the transferee of the title.

faqs.q: How long do I have to grieve my Burlington assessment?
faqs.a: 14 calendar days from the date on the Change of Assessment Notice. Hearings before the Board of Assessors are typically held in the third week of May.

faqs.q: Do Burlington rental owners need to register their rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The Minimum Housing Ordinance requires registration under Sec. 18-15 of the city code, and the Permitting and Inspections Department runs the process.

faqs.q: What is the Burlington weatherization ordinance?
faqs.a: It requires high energy use rental buildings, those above 50,000 BTU per square foot per year, to complete an audit and weatherization work with a BPI-certified contractor. Fees and fines apply if the work is late.
